headline: Ronaldo quits Portugal after 23 years and 146 goals.
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, said Thursday he will not play for Portugal again. He scored a record 146 goals in 234 games over 23 years, and Portugal won its first major title, Euro 2016, with him. His last game was a 1-0 win over Wales on September 24; he left camp after coach Jorge Jesus benched him. He keeps playing for Al-Nassr.
cover_answer: No. Only for Portugal. He still plays for his club.
table_question: Should you quit when the coach stops picking you?

5-7.script: Cristiano Ronaldo, the famous soccer player, said he won't play for his country, Portugal, anymore. He wore the number 7 shirt for 23 years, three of your whole lifetimes, and scored 146 goals in it. Now he's handing the shirt to the next player. He'll still play for his club team.
5-7.why: The shirt handed on is something they can picture. Twenty-three years is three of their lifetimes; that is the number that lands.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them a shirt handed to the next player and a number in their own life: 23 years is three of theirs. The coach stays off this card; one vivid feature becomes the event, and it should be the shirt. Expect "was he the best?" Portugal's federation says so.

8-12.script: Ronaldo's last Portugal game was September 24. Coach Jorge Jesus benched him and said he'd stay benched, so Ronaldo left camp. Thursday he retired. Before him Portugal reached three World Cups ever; with him, every one. A relay baton: run your leg, then hand it on.
8-12.why: Benched, left camp, retired: in order. The baton is the handover. At ten they can read one chain two ways.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script gives the chain in order: benched, left camp, retired. The baton gives them the handover reading, the chain the walkout, and both are true. Expect "was he right to leave?" The coach said he was welcome back. Ask what they'd do at 41 with no place in the team.

13-17.script: Is this a retirement or a walkout? Ronaldo left Portugal's camp after Jorge Jesus benched him; his last game was September 24, and on Thursday he quit by video. Second: he's 41, on 985 goals, chasing 1,000 at Al-Nassr. When the numbers are the point, who decides when you stop, you or the coach?
13-17.why: 23 years, then a walkout when benched. Who decides when you're done?
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: Ronaldo gave Portugal 23 years and a first title, and he walked out when a coach benched him. The script asks them to hold both, then turns it on them: who decides when you are done? Expect "would you have benched him?" Say what you think; they're testing if you'll argue honestly.

5-7.a: No. Only for Portugal. He still plays for his club, Al-Nassr, and wants 1,000 goals.

8-12.a: Benched, told he'd stay benched. He left camp, then quit.
Portugal's federation says so. 146 goals and 234 games are records.

13-17.q: Was that a retirement or a walkout?
13-17.a: Both. Benched, left camp, quit. The coach says the door is open.

13-17.q: Should the coach have started him?
13-17.a: The article doesn't say why. What does a coach owe a legend?
